zh-TW.long_thesis_markdown:
## 假日固定收益簡報

美國固定收益市場於 7 月 3 日星期五因美國獨立紀念日補假休市，符合 SIFMA 全日休市建議。當日沒有正常交易時段，也沒有美國固定收益市場的當日價格發現。相關資訊期間始於 7 月 3 日亞洲早盤，止於 7 月 6 日亞洲早盤，介於星期四提前收市與星期一恢復正常交易之間。期間內的發展可能影響市場重開，但不能解讀為 7 月 3 日美國公債的價格變動。

這段期間最重要的發展，是伊朗相關能源衝擊消退後，全球貨幣政策風險進一步分歧。油價下跌與美國聘僱轉弱，降低近期進一步緊縮的急迫性；多位歐洲央行官員也認為，6 月升息目前已經足夠。不過，這場衝擊已墊高主要經濟體控制通膨的門檻；財政擴張、人工智慧投資及央行減少政策指引，也使長天期債券的風險補償持續面臨上行壓力。因此，美國市場星期一重開時，必須同時消化近期能源壓力減輕，以及政策路徑仍具限制性且分歧異常擴大的局面。

日本則構成主要反向力量。正產出缺口、日圓疲弱與日本公債承壓，使政策正常化風險持續存在，即使油價下跌已在邊際上減輕輸入性通膨。中國減少政府債券買進，同時增設更精準的隔夜流動性工具，顯示政策著重支持資金融通，並不代表願意無限制承接存續期間風險。美國總統 Donald Trump 的盟友再次試圖重塑聯準會，另增制度面不確定性。這些發展使市場重開時，不僅對成長與通膨數據敏感，也將檢驗政策反應函數的可信度。

## 全球利率、信用與主權債發展

歐洲最清楚顯示，能源通膨降溫正在改變近期政策討論。法國、德國與義大利通膨普遍減速，帶動歐元區通膨降至 2.8%，低於預期。歐洲央行管理委員會委員 Emmanuel Moulin 表示，油價快速下跌，使央行在 6 月一致決議升息 25 個基點至 2.25% 後，處於更有利的位置；他也強調，當時並未將升息定位為新一輪緊縮循環的起點。Joachim Nagel 仍主張保持警覺，Gabriel Makhlouf 則重申對 2% 通膨目標的承諾。食品、服務與薪資是否出現落後轉嫁，因而成為延長暫停升息的主要限制。

Christine Lagarde 更明確地捍衛 6 月升息決定。她表示，管理委員會當時的選擇正確，因為外部供給衝擊已由能源擴散至其他項目，核心通膨也由 2.2% 升至 2.5%。第 2 輪效應雖尚未出現，仍是後續必須監測的風險。其後達成停火且油價下跌，改變的是近期風險分布，並未否定會議當時掌握的資訊。這項差異對德國公債尤其重要：能源壓力減輕可讓歐洲央行延長觀望期，但間接通膨效應已經浮現，加上央行預測 2027 年通膨仍高於目標，撤回 6 月升息的門檻仍高。

成長與外部收支數據，則限制了有利於存續期間的動能。法國 5 月製造業產出下降 1.0%，前月增幅修正為 0.6%，主要受到運輸設備，以及電機、電子與電腦產品疲弱拖累。整體工業產出下滑 0.1%；但採礦、能源與供水產出上升 3.2%，因此數據並非全面轉弱。歐盟第 1 季經常帳盈餘擴大至 €1,134億，相當於 GDP 的 2.4%；服務與初次所得增強，抵銷了商品盈餘縮小的影響。法國生產轉弱支持央行耐心觀望，外部盈餘則不支持歐元區面臨全面融資壓力的判斷。

法國財政前景帶來另一類主權債存續期間風險。財政部長 Roland Lescure 希望將赤字降至接近 GDP 的 5%，較 2025 年的 5.1% 僅略有改善。總理 Sebastien Lecornu 警告，若未通過新財政法案，只能沿用既有法規，赤字可能升至 6.5%。2027 年預算不僅必須通過政黨分裂的國會，還面臨預定於 4 月舉行的總統大選，財政整頓可能延誤或失序。官員表示，發債與標售目前運作順暢，因此眼前問題並非能否進入市場融資，而是政治協商若無法建立可信的債務路徑，投資人未來將要求多高的風險溢價。

聯準會不確定性的焦點，已由下次利率決策轉向治理與政策溝通。6 月非農就業僅增加 57,000 人，先前數據又遭下修，已削弱立即升息的理由；不過，勞動參與率下降，使失業率下滑較難解讀。假日期間有報導指出，美國最高法院阻止罷免 Lisa Cook 後，政府盟友正研究其他罷免理事的方法，聯準會獨立性疑慮因而再起。主席 Kevin Warsh 減少依賴前瞻指引，也增添一層變數：政策訊號減少後，新公布數據對市場的影響可能放大；政治壓力則可能使外界質疑，央行是否會堅定因應通膨風險。

日本經濟呈現溫和超額需求，政策組合也承受明顯壓力。日本央行估計，第 1 季產出缺口為 0.53%，略低於先前的 0.57%，資本與勞動均為正貢獻；潛在成長率估值則由 0.66% 上調至 0.69%。不過，日本央行提醒，兩項指標都對估算方法相當敏感。財務大臣片山皋月重申，政府已準備因應失序的匯率波動；她並將日本殖利率上升歸因於美國政策訊號、美國勞動數據疲弱及國內標售表現不佳。10 年期日本公債殖利率升至 2.81%，創 1996 年以來新高，顯示油價下跌仍不足以消除市場對財政、匯率及買方基礎的疑慮。

中國的流動性政策著重精準調控，而非透過債券市場全面寬鬆。中國人民銀行 6 月淨買入人民幣100億元政府債券，低於 5 月的人民幣500億元，創 9 個月最低。新設的隔夜公開市場操作，讓政策制定者可透過更短天期工具調節資金，減少以買進政府債券挹注長期流動性的必要。這套做法既可維持資金充裕，也能避免殖利率過度下滑；同時明確區隔支持走緩的國內經濟，與不計代價承接存續期間風險。

初級信用市場的融資管道仍然暢通，更重要的訊號來自潛在供給的結構與時點。CVC 計畫在夏季過後發行 €12億高收益債券，用以取代收購義大利食品配料製造商 Irca 時採用的銀行過橋融資，並搭配一筆循環信用額度。歐洲市場目前仍以再融資與重新定價交易為主，這筆發行將增加槓桿收購相關供給，儘管投資級以下債券需求仍具韌性。ICICI Bank 另考慮在未來幾週內，透過全球中期票據計畫發行至少 $5億，並運用印度央行為吸引境外資金而提供的外匯交換優惠。兩筆交易都尚未確立最終成交條件，但均顯示借款人正準備把握融資窗口。

新興市場的通膨與融資環境仍高度分化。土耳其 6 月消費者物價指數月增 0.99%、年增 32.11%；但食品通膨達 35.45%，住宅與公用事業通膨更達 45.14%，顯示單靠能源價格下跌，未必足以穩定通膨下降趨勢。另一方面，美國政策與美元的不確定性升高後，投資人已將利差交易的融資貨幣由美元分散至歐元、加幣與日圓。此舉降低了對單一融資貨幣的依賴；但聯準會若重現緊縮動能，仍可能壓縮利差，並使高殖利率主權債的融資環境收緊。巴西則為非正式工作者推出新的信貸與債務協商支持，引發財政與貨幣政策能否協調的疑問，儘管官員主張相關措施不會削弱貨幣政策的限制性。

殖利率曲線反映投資人對近期政策與長期財政風險的不同判斷。在最近一個完成的英國交易時段，英國公債 2 年期與 10 年期殖利率差擴大至 66 個基點，創 3 月中旬以來最陡收盤水準，曲線也比美國與德國同類曲線更陡。殖利率處於高檔時，資產管理機構願意持有短天期債券；但退休基金需求減弱，加上下屆政府的預算細節未定，使其不願延長存續期間。因此，曲線趨陡反映的是期限溢價與買方基礎限制，不只是市場提高對英國央行近期寬鬆的預期。這是延續至假日資訊期間的海外市場背景，並非美國固定收益市場的當日價格發現。

假日期間的跨資產走勢提供市場重開線索，但不構成美國固定收益市場的收盤價。Nasdaq 100 期貨上漲 1.2%，亞洲股市上漲約 2%，黃金上漲 1.2% 至約 $4,170；市場首次完全定價聯準會升息 25 個基點的時點，也由 10 月延後至 12 月。Brent 原油維持在 $72 以下，市場持續評估荷姆茲海峽航運是否暢通，以及美國與伊朗談判的進展。整體走勢顯示，市場對近期政策與能源風險的焦慮減輕，人工智慧題材也重新帶動風險偏好。這些變化屬於星期一的開盤條件，不能用來解釋並不存在的星期五美國公債走勢。

## 下一個開市交易日觀察

美國首波總體經濟數據將於 7 月 6 日星期一美東時間上午 10:00 公布，包括 ISM 服務業指數與紐約聯準銀行全球供應鏈壓力指數。星期二將公布 5 月貿易數據及 6 月消費者預期調查；6 月 16 至 17 日的聯邦公開市場委員會會議紀要，則於星期三下午 2:00 公布。若服務業活動轉弱、價格降溫且物流壓力受控，非農就業成長疲弱所釋出的訊號將延伸至 2 年期至 5 年期的政策敏感區段。反之，若需求仍具韌性或價格壓力再起，尤其會議紀要顯示決策官員廣泛支持 2026 年升息，市場將重新採取更偏緊縮的解讀，並質疑能源壓力減輕能否持續支撐市場重開。

美國財政部公布的發債日程，分別檢驗殖利率曲線前端的現金需求與指標長天期券的承接能力。星期一將標售 $920億的 91 天期國庫券及 $790億的 182 天期國庫券；星期二另將標售 $900億的 42 天期國庫券、$520億的 364 天期國庫券，以及 $580億的 3 年期公債。星期三將增額發行 $390億、票面利率 4.375% 的 10 年期公債，星期四再增額發行 $220億、票面利率 5.000% 的 30 年期公債。投標倍數、投標人配售結構及標售後表現，將顯示假日交割週期的影響僅限於現金管理，還是已擴及長端期限溢價。投資人廣泛參與可緩和供給疑慮；交易商承接比例偏高或債券持續走弱，則會加深疑慮。

日本後續數據將檢驗，正產出缺口是否正轉化為持續的所得與通膨壓力。5 月初步勞動數據將於 7 月 7 日公布，之後還有日本央行 6 月操作、政府交易及 5 月消費指數；日本央行地區經濟報告則於 7 月 9 日發布。若現金所得穩健、實質薪資改善且各地價格壓力更加普遍，即使油價下跌，政策正常化仍可能需要繼續推進；日本公債存續期間與日圓對此最為敏感。反之，若家庭所得或消費疲弱，且數據顯示流動性變化大多源於資產負債表運作，將削弱偏鷹解讀，並降低日本對全球期限溢價的推升作用。

## Holiday Fixed-Income Brief

U.S. fixed-income markets were closed on Friday, July 3, for U.S. Independence Day (observed), consistent with SIFMA’s full-close recommendation. There was no regular U.S. fixed-income session and no same-day U.S. fixed-income price discovery. The relevant information window runs from Asia morning on July 3 through Asia morning on July 6, after Thursday’s early close and before regular trading resumes Monday. Developments in that interval can shape the reopening, but they cannot be assigned to a July 3 Treasury move.

The window’s primary development was a widening divergence in global monetary-policy risks as the Iran-related energy shock faded. Lower oil and soft U.S. hiring reduced the urgency of additional near-term tightening, and several ECB voices judged June’s increase sufficient for now. The shock has nevertheless left a higher inflation hurdle across major economies, while fiscal expansion, artificial-intelligence investment and reduced central-bank guidance keep longer-duration compensation exposed. Monday’s U.S. reopening must therefore reconcile easier near-term energy pressure with policy paths that remain restrictive and unusually dispersed.

The main counterforce came from Japan, where a positive output gap, a weak yen and pressure in government bonds kept normalization risk alive even as lower oil reduced imported inflation at the margin. China also reduced sovereign-bond purchases while adding a more precise overnight liquidity tool, signaling support for funding without endorsing unlimited duration demand. Renewed attempts by President Donald Trump’s allies to reshape the Federal Reserve added a separate institutional uncertainty. Together, those developments leave the reopening sensitive to both the growth-and-inflation data and the credibility of the policy reaction function.

## Global Rates, Credit, And Sovereign Developments

Europe supplied the clearest evidence that energy disinflation is changing the near-term policy debate. Euro-area inflation slowed to 2.8%, below expectations, after broad deceleration in France, Germany and Italy. ECB Governing Council member Emmanuel Moulin said the rapid oil decline placed the central bank in a better position after June’s unanimous 25-basis-point increase to 2.25%, and emphasized that the move was not presented as the start of a new tightening cycle. Joachim Nagel still urged vigilance, while Gabriel Makhlouf stressed the commitment to the 2% target. The split turns delayed pass-through into food, services and wages into the decisive limitation on an extended pause.

Christine Lagarde defended the June increase more explicitly. She said the Governing Council had made the right choice because the external supply shock was already spreading beyond energy and core inflation had accelerated from 2.2% to 2.5%; second-round effects had not materialized, but remained the risk to monitor. The subsequent ceasefire and oil decline changed the near-term distribution rather than invalidating the information available at the meeting. That distinction matters for Bunds: less energy pressure can extend a pause, while observed indirect effects and the ECB’s above-target 2027 projection keep the threshold for reversing June’s move high.

Growth and external-balance data qualified that duration-friendly impulse. French manufacturing output fell 1.0% in May after a revised 0.6% increase, led by weakness in transport equipment and electrical, electronic and computer goods. Total industrial output slipped 0.1%, although mining, energy and water supply rose 3.2%, preventing a uniformly weak signal. The EU’s Q1 current-account surplus widened to €113.4 billion, or 2.4% of GDP, as stronger services and primary income outweighed a smaller goods surplus. Softer French production supports patience, whereas the external surplus limits the case for broad euro-area funding stress.

France’s fiscal outlook created a different sovereign-duration risk. Finance Minister Roland Lescure is seeking to bring the deficit close to 5% of GDP, only a modest improvement from 5.1% in 2025. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu warned that reliance on rolled-over legislation without a new finance bill could push the deficit to 6.5%. The 2027 budget must navigate a fragmented parliament and a presidential election due in April, leaving consolidation vulnerable to delay or disorder. Officials said issuance and auctions were functioning well, so the immediate issue is not market access; it is the future premium required if political compromise fails to produce a credible debt path.

Federal Reserve uncertainty shifted from the next decision toward governance and communication. June payroll growth of 57,000 and downward revisions had already softened the case for an immediate increase, even though lower participation complicated the fall in unemployment. During the holiday window, reporting that administration allies were exploring further ways to remove governors after the Supreme Court blocked the effort against Lisa Cook reopened the independence question. Chair Kevin Warsh’s reduced reliance on forward guidance adds another layer: fewer policy signals may make incoming data more influential, while political pressure could raise concern about how firmly inflation risks will be addressed.

Japan combined modest excess demand with visible pressure on its policy mix. The BOJ estimated a Q1 output gap of 0.53%, down slightly from 0.57%, with positive contributions from both capital and labor. Its potential-growth estimate increased to 0.69% from 0.66%, although the central bank cautioned that both measures are sensitive to methodology. Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama reiterated readiness to act on disorderly currency moves and linked the rise in Japanese yields to U.S. policy signals, weak U.S. labor data and a soft domestic auction. The 10-year JGB yield reached 2.81%, its highest since 1996, showing that lower oil has not displaced fiscal, currency and buyer-base concerns.

China’s liquidity stance pointed to control rather than broad easing through the bond market. The PBOC bought a net 10 billion yuan of government debt in June, down from 50 billion yuan in May and the smallest amount in 9 months. Its new overnight open-market operation gives policymakers a shorter instrument for steering funding, reducing the need to inject long-term liquidity through sovereign purchases. The combination can keep cash conditions ample while resisting excessive yield compression. It also separates support for a slowing domestic economy from a commitment to absorb duration at any price.

Primary credit remained accessible, with the more important signal coming from the structure and timing of prospective supply. CVC plans €1.2 billion of high-yield bonds after the summer to replace bank bridge financing for its acquisition of Italian food-ingredients producer Irca, alongside a revolving facility. The transaction would add leveraged-buyout supply to a European market still dominated by refinancing and repricing, even though speculative-grade demand has remained resilient. ICICI Bank is separately considering at least $500 million under its global medium-term-note program in coming weeks, using an RBI foreign-exchange swap concession designed to attract offshore capital. Neither planned deal establishes clearing terms yet; both show borrowers preparing to use open funding windows.

Emerging-market inflation and funding conditions stayed highly country-specific. Turkey’s June CPI rose 0.99% on the month and 32.11% from a year earlier, but food inflation of 35.45% and housing-and-utilities inflation of 45.14% show why cheaper energy alone may not anchor the disinflation path. At the same time, investors have diversified carry funding beyond the dollar into the euro, Canadian dollar and yen as uncertainty around U.S. policy and the dollar increased. That reduces dependence on a single funding currency, though a renewed Fed tightening impulse could still narrow rate differentials and tighten conditions for high-yielding sovereigns. Brazil added a fiscal-monetary question through new credit and debt-renegotiation support for informal workers, even as officials argued that the measures would not weaken monetary restraint.

The curve quantified investors' distinction between near-term policy and
long-run fiscal risk. In the latest completed UK session, the British
2-year/10-year gilt slope had widened to 66 basis points, its steepest close
since mid-March and steeper than comparable American and German curves. Asset
managers were willing to own short maturities at elevated yields, but remained
reluctant to extend duration while pension demand weakened and the next
government's budget details were unresolved. The steepening therefore
represented a term-premium and buyer-base constraint, not simply a larger
expectation of near-term BOE easing. This was overseas context carried into the
holiday information window, not same-day US fixed-income price discovery.

Holiday cross assets offered a reopening signal without creating a US fixed-income close. Nasdaq 100 futures rose 1.2%, Asian equities gained about 2%, and gold advanced 1.2% to roughly $4,170 as the first fully priced 25-basis-point Fed increase shifted back to December from October. Brent held below $72 while markets weighed continued Hormuz flows and US-Iran talks. The combination pointed to lower immediate policy and energy anxiety alongside renewed AI risk appetite; it belongs in Monday’s opening conditions, not as an explanation for a nonexistent Friday Treasury move.

## Next Open-Session Watch

The first U.S. macro sequence begins Monday, July 6, at 10:00 a.m. ET with ISM services and the New York Fed’s Global Supply Chain Pressure Index. May trade follows Tuesday, alongside the June Survey of Consumer Expectations, and the June 16–17 FOMC minutes arrive Wednesday at 2:00 p.m. Softer services activity, cooling prices and contained logistics pressure would extend the message from weak payroll growth into the 2- to 5-year policy channel. Resilient demand or renewed price pressure, especially if the minutes reveal broad support for a 2026 increase, would restore a more restrictive interpretation and weaken the case that energy relief can carry the reopening.

Treasury’s announced supply calendar separates front-end cash demand from benchmark-duration absorption. Monday brings $92 billion of 91-day bills and $79 billion of 182-day bills; Tuesday adds $90 billion of 42-day bills, $52 billion of 364-day bills and a $58 billion 3-year note. A $39 billion reopening of the 4.375% 10-year note follows Wednesday, then a $22 billion reopening of the 5.000% 30-year bond Thursday. Bid-to-cover, bidder allocation and post-auction performance will show whether the holiday settlement cycle is confined to cash management or reaches the long-end term premium. Broad participation would temper the supply concern; heavy dealer absorption or persistent cheapening would strengthen it.

Japan’s next releases determine whether the positive output gap is translating into durable income and inflation pressure. May provisional labor data arrive July 7, followed by June BOJ operations, government transactions and the May consumption index; the BOJ’s regional economic report is due July 9. Firm cash earnings, improving real wages and broader regional price pressure would raise the chance that normalization needs to proceed despite lower oil, with JGB duration and the yen most sensitive. Weak household income or consumption, combined with evidence that balance-sheet mechanics explain much of the liquidity change, would challenge the hawkish reading and reduce Japan’s contribution to global term-premium pressure.
